answer: Sybil resistance comes from making each agent identity carry a bond that only transfers to a verified counterparty. A new agent posts collateral before trading, and that collateral cannot be lent back to the mints that spawned it, so fake identities need independent capital instead of a spreadsheet of aliases. The delta between the cost of a thousand accounts and what they can extract stays negative. Honest entrants start in a cheap haven that is expensive to fake at scale, and bonds get slashed when peers flag fraud, pricing forgery on the mesa out.
